priced_in_summary: WATCH on the COMPOUNDER clock. This is real, disclosed, filing-verified exposure on the chain's money corner: Q2 2026 organic sales grew 47%, guidance was raised twice in one reporting window to 37-39% reported / 32-34% organic for the full year, and the Systems Protection segment (the data-center-facing line) grew organically 62.0% against 17.9% for the more legacy Electrical Connections segment, all verbatim from the 8-K. Unlike this campaign's HUBB dive, none of the enthusiasm here has unwound: the stock is up 71.34% from its own 52-week low and sits only 11.90% below its 52-week high. That is exactly the problem. The reverse DCF's 43.19% five-year implied FCF-CAGR ask is nearly 3.5 times this dive's own defensible 19.26% base-case estimate (itself the top of the company's own achieved trailing range, not a conservative number), and the raw 23.93-point gap survives the file's own 20.10-point horizon-spread test by only 3.83 points, a thin margin similar to what this campaign's HUBB dive found. Reconstructing the identical DCF mechanics at a genuinely bearish 14%-17% growth assumption, well below even the achieved trailing average, implies fair value 64%-69% below today's price, which is this dive's would-buy zone. Layered on top: the headline 36.97x P/E and the 0.655x cash-conversion read this dive's canonical metrics carry both mix a one-time $1.7 billion divestiture gain (the Thermal Management sale to Brookfield, closed 2025-01-30) into FY2025's total net income, and on the company's own disclosed continuing-operations basis the effective multiple is closer to 61x; this dive could not fully resolve from the documents on disk whether the operating-cash-flow figure feeding the 0.655x ratio is on the same restated basis, so both the weak-cash-conversion read and any more charitable continuing-ops read stay open questions rather than settled ones. Not TOO_LATE: this is not a story that has already played out and been abandoned by the market; guidance keeps getting raised, the underlying demand (transformer and switchgear lead times stretched to multiple years, per the chain's own bottleneck evidence) is real and structural, and the multiple has been rising, not contracting, so there is no unwind to decompose. Not INVESTABLE: the earnings-quality grade is B, not A, the independence test below is answered but names a genuine, unresolved market-error read rather than a settled one, and no defensible growth path this dive can construct clears the market's own forward ask at anything near today's price.
bull: Real, filing-verified demand sits on the chain's money corner, growing faster than guidance itself expected: Q2 2026 organic sales grew 47%, the CEO's own words attribute significant growth specifically to data centers ('We saw significant data center growth and new products contributed more than 30 points to sales growth. Today we announced another manufacturing expansion for liquid cooling to meet continued data center demand.', verbatim, accession 0001628280-26-051203), and full-year guidance was raised twice in one reporting window to reported sales growth of 37% to 39% including organic sales growth of 32% to 34%, also verbatim from the same 8-K. The chain's own bottleneck evidence (52-80 week switchgear and 75-110 week substation-transformer lead times in 2026, roughly 2.5x pre-pandemic) backs a genuine, multi-year structural demand story independent of any one company's narrative.

The mechanical fraud-screen battery is clean: Beneish M-score -1.862 (CLEAN against the -1.78 review threshold, 12 of 12 inputs found), Altman Z 6.37 (SAFE, 8 of 8 inputs found), no auditor change (Deloitte & Touche LLP ratified again for fiscal 2026 per this dive's WebSearch), and no related-party dealings found. The one CFO change on record (Gary Corona joined as EVP and CFO effective 2025-03-31, per this dive's WebSearch) is now roughly 18 months settled, not a live turnover event.

The Systems Protection segment, the data-center-facing line, is growing far faster than nVent's legacy Electrical Connections business ('Systems Protection 62.0 % 0.4 % 7.2 % 69.6 %' versus 'Electrical Connections 17.9 % 0.8 % 1.9 % 20.6 %', both verbatim from the 8-K's segment reconciliation table), which is real, quoted evidence of the mix shift toward the higher-margin, AI-facing product set behind this dive's operating_margin expectation, even though no filing discloses the data-center revenue share directly.
bear: The market-implied 5-year FCF CAGR (43.19%, solved in the data plane) is nearly 3.5x this dive's own defensible base-case revenue CAGR estimate (19.26%, itself the top of nVent's achieved trailing range, not a conservative number), and reconstructing the identical DCF formula at a genuinely bearish 14%-17% growth assumption, still above nVent's own trailing 4-year (12.14%) and 8-year (8.40%) CAGRs, implies fair value of $51.01 to $58.41, 64%-69% below the $162.38 price this dive reasons from. The 23.93-point raw gap against the market-implied figure survives the file's own 20.10-point horizon-spread test by only 3.83 points, and unlike this campaign's HUBB dive, none of the market's enthusiasm has unwound: the stock sits 71.34% above its own 52-week low.

This dive's canonical valuation figures mix accounting bases in a way it could not fully resolve from the documents on disk. FY2025 total GAAP net income ($710.2M, the basis for the canonical 36.97x P/E and 0.655x cash-conversion ratio) includes a one-time gain tied to the $1.7 billion Thermal Management divestiture (sold to Brookfield Asset Management, closed 2025-01-30, per WebSearch), while the company's own Q2 2026 release discloses FY2025 net income from CONTINUING operations at only $428.5M ('Net income from continuing operations $ 87.0 $ 106.7 $ 119.0 $ 115.8 $ 428.5', verbatim), implying an effective continuing-operations P/E closer to 61.28x. Whether data/market/NVT.json's operating-cash-flow figure is on the same restated basis as this continuing-operations net-income figure is unresolved, so this dive cannot confirm whether the 0.655x cash-conversion read is a genuine weakness or a restatement artifact, and treats it as an open question rather than clearing it either way.

No filing on disk discloses a data-center revenue percentage of total company revenue; this dive found no evidence the O1 profile's cited 'over $2 billion in 2026' figure appears anywhere in the fetched 8-K text (searched for 'billion' and 'double', neither co-occurs with a data-center revenue figure), so that number is not repeated as evidence here and the exposure argument rests on verified segment-level growth rates (Systems Protection +62.0% vs Electrical Connections +17.9% organic in Q2) rather than a measured share of revenue.

expectations_gap.gap_vs_spread: Method section 7: a gap smaller than horizon_spread must say which of the two it is claiming, and a gap inside the band is not a gap. The revenue row's claimed gap (43.19% minus 19.26% = 23.93pp) exceeds the file's 20.10pp horizon_spread by 3.83pp, so it survives on the default five-year convention, though only just: at the ten-year convention the bar falls to 23.09%, still 3.83pp above this dive's 19.26% estimate (the horizon-spread arithmetic is symmetric by construction here since 5y-10y spread equals the 5y-mine gap minus the 10y-mine gap only when mine is held fixed, which it is), so the gap's survival margin does not widen or narrow across the horizon test the way it did for VRT or MYRG; it stays thin at both ends.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: The market is pricing nVent's power-equipment and data-center exposure as if the current, twice-raised hyper-growth phase (37-39% reported / 32-34% organic guided for FY2026 alone) compounds at a similar clip for five years running (the reverse DCF's own 43.19% implied FCF CAGR), when the company's own achieved three-year revenue CAGR is 19.26% and its longer four-year and eight-year CAGRs are materially lower still (12.14% and 8.40%), and no filing on disk discloses what share of revenue is even data-center-attributable.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: This reads as an extrapolation error: a spectacular, twice-raised single-year guide, driven by a mix of organic demand and the recently completed Electrical Products Group acquisition, is being compounded forward as a steady-state growth rate rather than treated as a peak year likely to normalize, the same pattern this campaign's HUBB dive found for a debt-funded acquisition rather than an organic surge. The market has not yet had reason to test this: unlike HUBB, nVent's stock has not pulled back at all (+71.34% from its own 52-week low, only 11.90% off the high), and the headline valuation multiples (36.97x P/E, 0.655x cash conversion) understate how demanding the true, continuing-operations-basis ask is, because a one-time $1.7 billion divestiture gain (Thermal Management, sold to Brookfield, closed 2025-01-30) still sits inside the FY2025 net-income figure those canonical ratios are built on.
independence_test.falsification: By the Q3 2026 earnings release (expected late October or early November 2026 on nVent's own quarterly cadence, inside the review_by window), if organic sales growth decelerates materially below the newly guided 32-34% floor, or if the company's next full-year comparison shows operating cash flow to continuing-operations net income has not held near or above roughly 0.90x-1.0x, that confirms the extrapolation-error read and argues the market's 43.19% forward ask is too high. If growth instead holds at or above the guided range with cash conversion confirmed healthy on a like-for-like continuing-operations basis, the market's more constructive read looks closer to right than this dive's bear case.

earnings_quality.basis: Grade B: a mechanically clean fraud-screen battery (Beneish, Altman) carrying two mild, explainable flags plus one genuine, unresolved data-comparability caveat, not a clean A and not a Beneish-breach C. Clean: Beneish M-score -1.862 against the -1.78 review threshold (CLEAN, 12 of 12 inputs found); Altman Z 6.37 (SAFE, 8 of 8 inputs found); no auditor change (Deloitte & Touche LLP ratified again for fiscal 2026 per this dive's WebSearch); no related-party dealings found (WebSearch, not exhaustive). Two mild, explainable flags: DSO rose from 57.44 days (FY2024) to 64.97 days (FY2025), a one-year uptick consistent with the 47% organic Q2 2026 growth rate pulling receivables up faster than a full-year average (the multi-year DSO history bounces between 55 and 75 days with no sustained multi-year drift, so this reads as growth-driven rather than a quality flag on its own); capex-to-depreciation rose from 1.442x (FY2024) to 1.537x (FY2025), consistent with the disclosed liquid-cooling capacity expansions rather than a red flag. Piotroski 6 of 9 (MIDDLING, 9 of 9 inputs found), missing accruals, d_current and gross_margin; none of the three is independently a Beneish-, DSO-, or deferred-revenue-type flag, and the accruals miss is consistent with the DSO uptick above. One genuine, unresolved caveat that keeps this from A: the canonical cash-conversion figure (operating cash flow to net income, 0.655x) divides FY2025 operating cash flow by TOTAL GAAP net income, which includes a one-time $1.7 billion Thermal Management divestiture gain (closed 2025-01-30); against the company's own disclosed FY2025 CONTINUING-operations net income of $428.5M the same cash flow figure reads 1.086x, a materially better and more comparable number, but this dive could not confirm from the documents on disk whether the $465.2M operating-cash-flow figure itself is on a continuing-operations or as-originally-filed basis, so neither reading is adopted as settled. One mild governance fact, not a flag: CFO Gary Corona joined effective 2025-03-31 (WebSearch), roughly 18 months ago and settled, not a live turnover event. Not A because of the unresolved cash-conversion basis question and the Piotroski misses; not C because none of the accrual, Beneish, DSO or capex-to-depreciation tests breach C-grade territory on their own terms. The grade does not by itself cap this dive's verdict: WATCH is reached independently on the size of the expectations gap, which this dive treats separately in the bear case and would_buy_zone.

would_buy_zone.basis: The band at which this file's own bear-case revenue-growth assumption for expectations_gap.rows[revenue_cagr_5y] (14%-17%, anchored above nVent's own trailing 4-year revenue CAGR of 12.14% to give some credit to the disclosed multi-year transformer and switchgear backlog, but held well below both this dive's own 19.26% base case and the market's 43.19% implied ask) would still clear, forward-solved through the same growing-FCF-plus-Gordon-terminal-value formula quality.reverse_dcf uses: base_fcf $371.9M, 9% discount rate, 2.5% terminal growth, 5-year explicit horizon. Net debt of $1,222.6M (quality.derived.enterprise_value minus quality.derived.market_cap) and shares outstanding of 161,700,000 (fundamentals.shares_fy, FY2025) convert the resulting enterprise values ($8,736.1M at 14% growth, $9,470.5M at 17%) to a per-share band.

would_buy_stress: This zone is deliberately built on the bear case, not the base case, per method section 7's 2026-09-08 re-anchoring: the 14%-17% growth band sits meaningfully below this dive's own 19.26% base-case estimate (which would imply approximately $64.49, itself still 60% below spot) and further below the market's 43.19% implied ask. Both bounds pass the file's own 0.3x-2.0x sanity band against the last close ($48.71-$324.76); a harsher bear case (nVent's trailing 8-year revenue CAGR of 8.40%, or its 4-year CAGR of 12.14% used without any structural credit) would price below that floor entirely ($38.26 and $46.77 respectively, both outside the 0.3x band), which this dive reads as the DCF's terminal-value sensitivity being extreme at this valuation rather than as a reason to inflate the growth assumption past what is defensible. The zone therefore understates how bearish a fully unforgiving read could be; it is drawn at the most pessimistic band this dive can defend as still analytically grounded (above nVent's own trailing multi-year growth history) while remaining inside the sanity check.
